newsitem.title: USA: Mall group sees holiday sales up 4-5 percent.
newsitem.headline: Mall group sees holiday sales up 4-5 percent.

text.p: Sales at the nation's regional shopping malls for the first 10 days of the holiday season remain on target for a projected increase of between 4 percent and 5 percent over last year's levels, the International Council of Shopping Centres said Tuesday.
The council said sales in the malls surveyed in its study from Friday, Nov. 29 through Sunday, Dec. 8 were up 17.4 percent, compared with the first 10 days after Thanksgiving of 1995.
The council's database of 62 malls measures sales per square foot in more than 3,300 speciality stores, but it does not include department stores and other mall "anchors," the group said.
It said that the double-digit increase in sales was expected this holiday season because there are five fewer shopping days between Thanksgiving and Christmas than there were in 1995.
